subject: Media Literacy
title: Checking the Source
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Checking the Source.

hook.text: A professional-looking website claimed a celebrity died. Millions shared it. The celebrity was alive and well.

buildup.text: Checking the source means asking: who published this, and do they have a track record of accuracy?

discovery.text: Reliable sources have bylines, correction policies, editorial standards, and transparent ownership.

twist.text: Unreliable sources often mimic legitimate news design — professional layouts and serious-sounding names.

climax.text: The 'About Us' page tells you more about a news source's reliability than any single article.

punchline.text: Before trusting the story, investigate who's telling it.

quiz.question: What indicates a reliable news source?
options: Bylines, correction policies, and transparent ownership
